case1-revised.report:
The masks contain **two baseline retroperitoneal tumor instances and one follow-up instance**, linked by one **merging** event. The dominant left para-aortic component and a smaller right retrocaval/interaortocaval component are distinguishable at baseline. On follow-up, the enlarged tissue behind the aorta forms a broad continuous mass whose component boundary I cannot reliably distinguish. This instance/event interpretation has moderate confidence; the presence of abnormal retroperitoneal tissue is more certain than its subdivision.

| Input / local ID | Location | Native axial extent, inclusive | Approximate segmented volume |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz`, 1 | Left para-aortic component | z=89–116 | 55.1 mL |
| `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz`, 2 | Right retrocaval/interaortocaval component | z=100–125 | 23.5 mL |
| `/app/data/followup.nii.gz`, 1 | Confluent retroperitoneal mass | z=90–131 | 130.9 mL |

Both complete scan extents were reviewed with axial soft-tissue montages, contiguous targeted abdominal and lung slices, and supplementary coronal/sagittal views, including bone-window review. Contours were drawn from the images on the native grids and interpolated between reviewed contour planes using signed distances. Local attenuation filtering helped exclude opacified vessels and bone. Overlays were inspected and contours revised, particularly along the vena cava. No reference masks, external data, or downloaded models were used. Correspondence was based on anatomy and morphology, not equal voxel indices or label numbers.

Coordinates below are **approximate zero-based native voxel indices `(x,y,z)`**, not RAS world millimeters. B means `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz`; F means `/app/data/followup.nii.gz`.

| Uncertain candidate / boundary | Native location | Included / excluded and reason |
|---|---|---|
| Left para-aortic tissue | B `(280,260,103)`; F `(285,233,111)` | **Included**, B1 / F1. Bulky solid tissue in a nodal distribution, enlarging across visits; judged more likely tumor. |
| Right retrocaval tissue and cranial taper | B `(236,274,118)`; F `(236,248,122)` | **Included**, B2 / part of F1. Abnormally bulky tissue contiguous through multiple slices and larger later. Boundary with the diaphragmatic crus and the baseline interface with B1 are approximate. |
| Enlarged heterogeneous left thyroid | B `(279,256,216)`; F `(279,218,216)` | **Excluded**. Similar smooth multinodular enlargement with internal degeneration/calcification; judged more likely benign goiter. |
| Rounded uterine enhancement/enlargement | B `(263,273,44)`; F `(260,270,50)` | **Excluded**. Circumscribed uterine appearance with calcification and similar morphology; benign myometrial/fibroid tissue favored. |
| Right lower renal fluid-density abnormality | B `(177,255,96)`; F `(188,237,103)` | **Excluded**. Fluid-containing collecting-system/cystic appearance with renal parenchymal continuity, rather than a solid tumor. |
| Anterior lingular opacity | B approximately `(390,220,142)`; F `(380,188,146)` | **Excluded**. Thin linear/plate-like morphology on contiguous lung images favors scar or atelectasis. |

No additional findings were judged more likely tumor than normal or benign tissue. Three-millimeter slice thickness, partial-volume effects, and contact with vessels/crura limit boundary precision. No disappearance was inferred from field-of-view differences.

Representative evidence is in [the input/overlay comparison](../work/representative_evidence.png): baseline native slices **99, 109, 120** and follow-up native slices **102, 113, 125**. These show the inferior left component, the contacting/confluent region, and the superior right component, respectively. Other reviewed montages and scripts are retained in `/app/work/`.

Both saved masks were reloaded and verified as 3D `uint16`, with exact input shapes and affines. Every positive ID appears exactly once in `events.json`. Reproduction: `/app/work/finalize.py`; checks and measurements: `/app/work/validation.json`.

case2-image.report:
Paired CT lesion analysis

The image-based result is **one baseline lesion and two follow-up lesions**, all hepatic. Baseline ID 1 corresponds to follow-up ID 1 (`persistent`, with substantial enlargement). Follow-up ID 2 is `newly_appearing`. No merging or disappearing lesions were identified.

Both complete input volumes were surveyed with axial soft-tissue views, contiguous two-slice survey slabs, and additional lung-window views. Liver candidates were examined on individual adjacent axial slices and coronal/sagittal reformats. Lesions were delineated with manually specified slice-wise envelopes and locally constrained intensity segmentation, followed by contour review. Mild smoothing aided low-contrast boundary assessment; masks remain on the original native grids. No external images, annotations, pretrained models, or network resources were used.

All coordinates below are **zero-based native voxel indices `(x, y, z)`**, not RAS world millimeters. Axial slice index is `z`. `B` means `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz`; `F` means `/app/data/followup.nii.gz`. The scans have different origins, coverage, and slice spacing; correspondence was established anatomically, not by equating voxel indices or world coordinates.

| Finding | Native location / axial extent | Decision and uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| B, posterior right-liver mass | Center approximately `(176,295,435)`; mask z=422–446 | **Included, ID 1.** Reproducible rounded hypodense mass across planes. Low contrast makes its peripheral extent uncertain. |
| F, enlarged posterior right-liver mass | Center approximately `(160,260,552)`; mask z=531–571 | **Included, ID 1.** Same hepatic region and anatomical relationships as B ID 1. One continuous mass without distinguishable constituent lesions; reaches the hepatic surface superiorly. |
| F, small peripheral anterior right-liver focus | `(123,210,529)`; mask z=525–532 | **Included, ID 2.** Discrete round hypodensity on adjacent slices and sagittal views, without convincing vessel continuity or a visible baseline counterpart. A benign cyst remains possible, but tumor is favored in this image comparison. |
| B, broader inferior/lateral hepatic low attenuation | Around `(155,253,413)` | **Excluded.** Broad regional variation without a separable rounded mass; more consistent with parenchymal heterogeneity/artifact. |
| F, central round hepatic-region hypodensity | Around `(226,250,538)` | **Excluded.** Traces along the inferior vena cava rather than forming a separate mass. |
| F, smaller central hepatic dark focus | Around `(190,235,536)` | **Excluded.** Tubular/branching continuation on adjacent images favors a vessel. |
| B/F, anterior right-thigh skin/subcutaneous thickening | B approximately `(175,103,104)`; F approximately `(173,102,282)` | **Excluded.** Similar flat, irregular plaque and radiating strands at both visits, favoring scar-related change over a distinct tumor nodule. |

No additional finding was judged more likely tumor than normal or benign tissue. Small-lesion detection and precise borders remain limited by image noise and limited tissue contrast. The small follow-up lesion's event describes newly visible disease on these supplied images; microscopic prior presence cannot be assessed. No absence outside scan coverage was used to declare disappearance.

[Representative raw CT and mask contours](../work/representative_evidence.png) show **B axial slice 435**, **F axial slice 550**, and **F axial slice 529**, respectively. Detailed adjacent-slice contour reviews are preserved in [baseline_overlay.jpg](../work/baseline_overlay.jpg), [followup_overlay.jpg](../work/followup_overlay.jpg), and [followup_small_overlay.jpg](../work/followup_small_overlay.jpg). Additional surveys and multiplanar views are under `/app/work/`.

The estimated segmented volumes are B ID 1: 63.4 mL; F ID 1: 416.7 mL; F ID 2: 2.2 mL. These depend on the uncertain image-defined margins. Both NIfTI outputs use uint16 labels and exactly match their input shape and affine. Every positive ID appears once in `events.json`. Reproducible delineation and validation scripts are `/app/work/segment.py` and `/app/work/validate.py`; validation details are in `/app/work/validation.json`.

case2-context.report:
# Paired CT lesion analysis

The masks contain **one baseline lesion and two follow-up lesions**, all hepatic. The event assignments are one **persistent** lesion and one **newly_appearing** lesion. These are image-based judgments, not a clinical diagnosis or response category.

## Method

Reviewed the complete anatomical coverage of `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz` and `/app/data/followup.nii.gz` with axial overview sheets, focused adjacent-slice review, soft-tissue, liver, lung, brain and bone windows, and targeted sagittal/coronal reconstructions. No external images, annotations or pretrained models were used. Findings were matched using organ location and surrounding anatomy, not the markedly different world-coordinate origins.

Image-reviewed axial contours were interpolated using signed distances and rasterized on each original grid. Contours encompass the visible mass rather than only its darkest center. The two follow-up lesions are spatially distinct. The dominant mass is treated as one lesion at each visit because separate constituent tumors cannot be distinguished. Peripheral air was excluded where the follow-up mass approaches the liver surface. Scripts, contour definitions and review images are in `/app/work/`.

## Included lesions and correspondence

All coordinates below are **zero-based native voxel indices `(i,j,k)`**, not RAS world millimeters. Axial slice index is `k`. Centers are rounded mask centroids; slice ranges are inclusive.

| Input | ID | Location and center | Mask slices | Interpretation |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `baseline.nii.gz` | 1 | Posterior superior right hepatic lobe; `(177,297,434)` | 421–448 | Subtle, heterogeneous low-attenuation mass; included despite limited contrast. |
| `followup.nii.gz` | 1 | Same hepatic region; `(158,259,551)` | 530–571 | Larger, more conspicuous lobulated mass. Anatomical identity supports **persistent** correspondence with baseline ID 1. |
| `followup.nii.gz` | 2 | Anterolateral right hepatic lobe; `(123,204,529)` | 525–532 | Separate rounded low-attenuation focus, judged more likely tumor. No convincing baseline counterpart in the covered region; **newly_appearing**. |

No merging or disappearing event is asserted. Differences in scan coverage were not interpreted as disappearance.

## Uncertainty and excluded candidates

| Candidate / native location | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline dominant liver mass, `(177,297,434)` | Included, ID 1 | Reproducible focal abnormality across slices and planes, with a matching follow-up mass. Baseline margins have substantial uncertainty from noise and weak tissue contrast. |
| Follow-up small liver focus, `(123,204,529)` | Included, ID 2 | Rounded, spatially discrete lesion absent on baseline review. A benign cyst remains possible, but tumor is favored in this paired-image assessment. |
| Anterior hepatic focus: baseline `(190,199,406)`; follow-up `(182,165,524)` | Excluded | Small, sharply defined and similar across visits; benign cyst-like or vascular focus favored over tumor. |
| Right anterior thigh, follow-up `(160,108,283)` | Excluded | Plaque-like superficial soft tissue with surrounding reticular stranding; benign inflammatory/scar-like change favored over a discrete tumor. This is a morphological judgment; surgery or its timing is **not** established. |

The scans are noisy and lack conspicuous intravenous enhancement. Small lesions, especially intracranial or nearly isodense visceral lesions, may not be detectable. Estimated boundaries, particularly baseline liver margins, are approximate.

## Representative evidence and checks

- Baseline mass: `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz`, native axial slices **430, 433, 436, 439**; [contour overlay](../work/overlay_baseline_421.jpg).
- Matching follow-up mass: `/app/data/followup.nii.gz`, slices **542, 550, 558**; [contour overlay](../work/overlay_followup_534.jpg).
- Separate follow-up focus: `/app/data/followup.nii.gz`, slices **527–531**; [contour overlay](../work/overlay_followup_525.jpg).
- Excluded thigh candidate: `/app/data/followup.nii.gz`, slice **283**; [native coordinate view](../work/detail_followup_283.png).

Validation passed: both masks are 3D `uint16`, have exactly the respective input shape and affine, and use background 0. Every positive ID occurs exactly once in `events.json`; event cardinalities are valid. See `/app/work/validation.json` and `/app/work/validate.py`.

case1-original.report:
# Paired CT lesion analysis

The best-effort masks identify **one confluent retroperitoneal lesion in each examination** (local ID 1). Its left para-aortic, retro-aortic and interaortocaval portions are connected and are therefore represented as one instance. The matching location relative to the aorta, vena cava, vertebrae and renal vessels supports a **persistent** correspondence. This describes identity, not stable size. No other definite tumor focus was identified in the volume review.

Both complete input volumes were reviewed in axial soft-tissue views, with supplementary lung-window views and targeted coronal/sagittal reformats. Image-guided native axial contours were interpolated using signed distance fields, then refined with intensity-based vessel/fat exclusions and visual overlay checks. No external data or pretrained models were used. The outputs are uint16 masks on the original grids; shape, affine, qform and sform equality and complete event-ID coverage were verified.

| Input file | Local ID | Labeled native axial slices, inclusive | Approximate mask volume |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz` | 1 | 82–125 | 103.2 mL |
| `/app/data/followup.nii.gz` | 1 | 86–131 | 156.9 mL |

Representative evidence is saved in [paired_evidence.png](../work/paired_evidence.png), with unmarked CT and mask overlays. Its rows show `/app/data/baseline.nii.gz` at **k=100, 110, 120**, respectively, alongside `/app/data/followup.nii.gz` at **k=104, 114, 124**. These demonstrate the lower para-aortic portion, the confluent central portion, and the superior interaortocaval portion. [Orthogonal views](../work/orthogonal_evidence.png) show continuity. All displayed coordinates and slice numbers are **zero-based native voxel indices**, not RAS world millimeters.

Localization and correspondence are more certain than the exact boundary. Margins against the vena cava, pancreas, psoas and diaphragmatic crura are partly indistinct; superior/inferior partial-volume boundaries are approximate. Small or isoattenuating lesions could be missed. Nodular thyroid tissue (baseline k=214; follow-up k=218) was not confidently attributable to tumor and was excluded. These are image-based, unvalidated annotations.

Reproducible contour definitions, segmentation/rendering scripts, full-volume review sheets and `validation.json` are retained under `/app/work/`. Run `python /app/work/segment.py` and `python /app/work/finalize.py` to regenerate the masks, event file and representative views.
